newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arcadia, Sipa climb on Mount Olympus news.
newsitem.headline: Arcadia, Sipa climb on Mount Olympus news.

text.p: Shares in Sipa International Resources Ltd and Arcadia Minerals Ltd jumped 15 percent and 25 percent respectively in active early Monday trade after Arcadia announced strong drilling results from their Mount Olympus joint venture in Western Australia.
Sipa rose nine cents to 55 cents on over 690,000 shares traded, while Arcadia rose 20 cents to 99 cents on volume of 50,000 shares traded.
Arcadia said it had extended the Mount Olympus lode in Western Australia because of the results, which included one intercept of 105 grams/tonne for a metre.
The Dublin Hill joint venture is owned 30 percent by Arcadia and 70 percent owned by Sipa, its would-be suitor, which is currently offering five of its shares for every three Arcadia shares.

By 11.45 a.m. (0045 GMT), Sipa shares were seven cents higher at 55 cents on turnover of 888,720 shares, while Arcadia shares remained 20 cents higher at 99 cents after only five trades totalling 50,000 shares.
